page.title: File services
page.webdavDesc: Reuses the main HTTP port (80) under /dav; supports Windows drive mapping
page.sftpDesc: Standalone SFTP endpoint; works with sshfs mounts and clients like WinSCP
page.ftpDesc: Standalone FTP endpoint; works with clients like FileZilla and resumable downloads
page.ossDesc: Reuses the main HTTP port (80) under /oss; S3-compatible API for rclone and S3 SDKs
page.alistDesc: Reuses the main HTTP port (80) with an AList v3 compatible API (/api + /d raw links); token clients log in, TVBox-style players need guest access

form.readOnlyHint: When on, only reading is allowed (browse, download, stream); upload, mkdir, rename, move and delete are rejected. Takes effect immediately
form.allowGuestHint: Lets players that never log in (TVBox-style) browse and stream as the public account below; this is an identity switch, unrelated to read-only mode — anonymous writes are always rejected
form.guestUserHint: Guests browse as this account: every file under it becomes publicly readable, so keep only shareable media there
form.guestPasswordHint: When on, the client's password field must be this account's login password — blank or wrong means no listing. When off, guests browse anonymously as before
form.guestUserInvalid: The current public account no longer exists or is disabled; select another one
form.bindAddressHint: 0.0.0.0 listens on all interfaces; recommended for LAN use only

dialog.enableDesc: Once enabled, clients can access your files through this protocol. Continue?
dialog.disableDesc: All client connections will be dropped immediately. Continue?

webdav.windows: Windows: enable the WebClient service, then run net use Z: http://<host>/dav in Explorer or a command prompt
webdav.rclone: rclone: create a WebDAV remote with rclone config, set the URL to http://<host>/dav, and use your drive credentials
webdav.basic: Credentials are your drive login; Basic auth is plain HTTP — put an HTTPS reverse proxy in front for production
webdav.lock: Write locks (LOCK/UNLOCK) are supported: Office can edit and save in place; locks live in memory, expire after 1 hour by default, and drop on service restart

sftp.winscp: WinSCP / FileZilla: choose SFTP, port {{port}}, and use your drive credentials
sftp.readonly: SFTP supports sequential writes only; random writes, hard links and symlinks fail explicitly

ftp.client: ftp client: ftp <host> {{port}} (or lftp / Explorer ftp://<host>:{{port}})
ftp.filezilla: FileZilla / WinSCP: choose FTP (plain), port {{port}}, and use your drive credentials
ftp.pasv: Passive data ports 50000-50100 must be allowed by the firewall; downloads support resume, uploads do not
ftp.security: FTP is a plaintext protocol for LAN use only; prefer SFTP or WebDAV over HTTPS when exposed

alist.client: TV box players: choose AList as the drive type, set the URL to http://<host>:{{port}} (no path) and the initial path to /; put the public account's login password in the password field (required when folder password is on, otherwise leave it blank) — these clients never log in and use it to gain anonymous browsing. Guest access with a public account must be enabled
alist.playback: Logged-in clients play via signed /d links (12h); guests play unsigned /d links authorized as the public account. Range requests avoid re-downloading on seek
alist.clients: rclone / AList desktop: exchange your drive credentials for a token via POST /api/auth/login (standard AList v3); guest access is not needed
alist.readonly: Read-only mode is recommended: a TV box only needs read access; when on, mkdir/rename/move/copy/remove/put return 403
alist.guestPassword: With folder password on, it is checked on list, search and get only; wrong attempts count toward the shared account+IP brute-force lockout. Playback links carry no password, so anyone with a full path can still stream — keep sensitive files out of the public account

oss.client: rclone: create an S3 remote with rclone config, set the endpoint to http://<host>/oss, region us-east-1, and use the key pair below
oss.keys: SDK/tools use the fixed bucket name gfs with path-style addressing (e.g. /oss/gfs/folder/file.txt)
oss.prefix: SigV4 authentication: requests must carry an AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 Authorization header (rclone, AWS SDKs, Cyberduck, WinSCP S3 all support it natively)
oss.semantics: Deletes go to the recycle bin and are recoverable; bucket management, ACL and anonymous access are not supported; revoked keys stop working immediately

keys.title: Access keys
keys.empty: No keys yet. Create a SigV4 credential pair to connect S3 clients.
keys.createDesc: Issue an Access Key / Secret Key pair for S3-compatible clients.
keys.createdDesc: The Secret Key is shown only once — copy and store it now; it cannot be viewed again.
keys.revokeDesc: Clients using this key lose access immediately and this cannot be undone. Continue?
keys.deleteDesc: This revoked key record will be permanently removed from the list and cannot be restored. It is already unusable for access. Continue?
